description.value: This study investigated emotional interference, BOLD activation, and right-insula functional connectivity in male adolescents with Internet gaming disorder compared with healthy controls during an emotional Stroop Match-to-Sample task.

spans.text: This study tested the hypothesis that adolescents with Internet gaming disorder would be more disturbed by the emotional interference and demonstrate compromised dorsal anterior cingulate cortex (dACC) activation during a Stroop Match-to-Sample task.

value: the hypothesis that adolescents with Internet gaming disorder would be more disturbed by the emotional interference and demonstrate compromised dACC activation during the Stroop Match-to-Sample task
It was hypothesized that the functional connectivity of the dACC would be disrupted in adolescents with Internet gaming disorder.

value: The healthy control group demonstrated significant BOLD responses to emotionally interfering angry faces in the dACC, primary motor cortex, superior temporal sulcus, and posterior parietal cortex, whereas the Internet gaming disorder group did not show these responses. The dACC and dorsal attention network were more strongly activated in the healthy control group, indicating compromised prefrontal cognitive control in adolescents with Internet gaming disorder.

The stronger activation of the right anterior insula was interpreted as related to weaker activation of the dorsal attention network, and fusiform gyrus activation indicated failure to ignore the emotional interfering angry faces.
